name: Fixed-size sliding window
whenToUse: The standard answer: one pass, a running sum, no extra memory and no division.

card.signals: "sub-arrays of size k" (contiguous, and the window size never changes) and a test on each window (average ≥ threshold). Two neighbouring windows share k − 1 elements, so most of the work is the same.
card.pattern: a fixed-size window. Build the first window of k elements, then slide it one step at a time: one element enters on the right, one leaves on the left. Each element is added once and dropped once, so the scan is O(n).
card.coreIdea: keep total, the sum of the window. Every window has length k, so average ≥ threshold is the same as total ≥ min_sum = threshold × k. Count each window that passes this test.

invariant: After each slide, the window arr[left..right] has exactly k elements, and total is their sum.

legend.text: left: left edge of the window
